sees: frame 1: A woman in a red coat with a crossbody bag and dark ponytail stands in front of library bookshelves, looking worried or sad, holding a small dark blue open book at her side.
frame 2: Same woman, now with a stern or unimpressed face (heavy-lidded eyes, flat mouth). The small dark blue book is now resting on a small wooden stool next to her.
frame 3: The background has changed to a desk area with computer monitors. The woman looks worried or wide-eyed. A large dark blue open book floats or lies open on the desk behind her, unattended.
actor: a woman with a dark ponytail in a red coat with a crossbody bag
before: in frame 1, the woman holds the small open book in her hand at her side
after: in frame 3, the book is no longer held; it is a large open book lying on a desk behind/beside her, apart from her
change: the woman puts the book down (first on a stool, then it ends up large and open on a desk away from her); her expression goes from worried to unimpressed to worried again, and the setting moves from library shelves to an office desk with screens
consequence: the book is being set aside or left unread; her work or writing is put down and ignored, suggesting nobody picks it up and reads it
message: The narrator is saying that people put down and ignore a long document or book, so nobody wants to read what you wrote.
